title: Kano Model
subtitle: Understand what truly delights customers and what just keeps them from leaving
useWhen: You're adding features and your product satisfaction scores aren't improving. Customers say they want something but when you build it, it doesn't seem to move the needle. You're not sure where to invest next.
howToUse: Developed by Professor Noriaki Kano at Tokyo University of Science in 1984, the Kano Model classifies product features into three types: Basic Needs (expected, their absence causes dissatisfaction but their presence goes unnoticed), Performance Needs (more is better these features directly drive satisfaction), and Excitement Needs (unexpected, their presence delights, their absence is not missed). Features also evolve over time: today's excitement becomes tomorrow's basic need. AI can help you classify your features and decide where to invest.
steps: List all your current and planned features before prompting.
Classify each feature honestly, most teams overestimate how many are Excitement features.
Ensure Basic Needs are fully met before investing in Excitement features.

Identify features that used to be Excitement and have become Basic these must beflawless. Most teams skip Basic Needs and invest in Excitement features, then wonder why satisfaction scores don't move. A delighted customer who hits a broken basic feature will churn regardless.
origin: Noriaki Kano, Tokyo University of Science — Kano Model, 1984
promptBody:
Act as a product strategy advisor using the Kano Model.
My product            :  [DESCRIBE WHAT IT DOES]
Target customer   :  [WHO USES IT AND IN WHAT CONTEXT]
I will list my features. Classify each as:
BASIC NEED                   :  Expected — absence causes frustration
PERFORMANCE NEED  :  More = better, directly drives satisfaction
EXCITEMENT NEED      :  Unexpected delight — creates love for product
Features to classify        :  [LIST YOUR FEATURES ONE PER LINE]
After classifying              :  which Excitement feature should I build next to create
maximum delight? Which Basic Need am I most at risk of failing on?
Kano Model of Customer Satisfaction
Basic Needs
Essential features that prevent
dissatisfaction

Features that improve product
functionality

proTip:
The most dangerous Kano insight is the feature that was Excitement two years ago and is
now Basic Need. Your competitors have copied it. Your customers expect it. If it's not
flawless now, it's actively hurting you. Run this audit every six months.
